title: Accounting Basis for the Value Released from Travel Credit — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A traveller may put the credit standing in their own name towards an Air Ticket Fare Brands itinerary they are holding, and the movement is made by the traveller rather than on their behalf, because the credit is their property.

## 1. The standing value

Value is taken off a traveller's credit only once a voucher carrying that value stands on the booking whose cancellation produced it.

The standing value is read as every voucher raised against that booking, less whatever has already been taken off those vouchers.

## 2. The three shares

2.1 **The release share.** The low release share of the standing value is released at one movement: 0.9 of it, being 90 percent.

2.2 **The age share.** The days the credit has stood unused are counted from the day the booking's ticket was issued to today. Where the most recent voucher on the booking was raised less than 1 month ago and the days the credit has stood unused are 90 or fewer, the whole of that figure is carried forward — a share of 1; where the most recent voucher was raised less than 1 month ago and those days exceed 90, the aged age share of it is carried forward, 0.97, being 97 percent; and in every other case the stale age share of it is carried forward, 0.93, being 93 percent.

2.3 **The release-record share.** The repeat release share of that figure is then carried forward: 0.9 of it, being 90 percent.

| Most recent voucher on the booking | Days the credit has stood unused | Age share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| raised less than 1 month ago | 90 or fewer | 1 |
| raised less than 1 month ago | more than 90 | 0.97 |
| raised 1 month ago or more | any | 0.93 |

## 3. How the figure is assembled

The release share, the age share and the release-record share are multiplied against the standing value in that order, giving the gross release, and the reissue fee of the fare brand that produced the credit and the cover deduction are then taken off that gross release rather than off any share before it.

The reissue fee of the fare brand that produced the credit is taken off the gross release in full. Nothing is taken off for protection cover: the cover deduction stands at 0.00 USD.

The value released never falls below zero, and the result is rounded to the nearest cent.

## 4. Worked figure, on hypothetical inputs

A booking carrying one voucher of 667.24 USD with nothing yet taken off it, that voucher raised 4 months ago, the ticket issued 300 days ago, and held in a brand whose reissue fee is a hypothetical 50.00 USD.

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| the standing value: one voucher of 667.24 USD, nothing taken off | 667.24 USD |
| the release share of 0.9 | 600.516 |
| the age share: the voucher was raised 4 months ago, so 0.93 | 558.47988 |
| the release-record share of 0.9, giving the gross release | 502.631892 |
| the brand's reissue fee of 50.00 USD taken off the gross release | 452.631892 |
| the cover deduction of 0.00 USD taken off the same gross release | 452.631892 |
| held at nothing were it lower, and rounded to the nearest cent | 452.63 USD |
